title: The essential image of closed direct image
statement:
For a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ with complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ that is quasi-compact as a morphism, a pro-etale module sheaf $F$ lies in the image of $i_*$ if
and only if $j^*F=0$. For such a sheaf the canonical unit $F\to i_*i^*F$ is
an isomorphism. Here the coefficient convention is that of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]: fix a sheaf $A_X$ of commutative rings on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, sheaves $A_Z,A_U$ on $Z_{\mathrm{proet}},U_{\mathrm{proet}}$, and isomorphisms $c_i:i^{-1}A_X\xrightarrow{\sim}A_Z$, $c_j:j^{-1}A_X\xrightarrow{\sim}A_U$. The functors $i^*,i_*,j^*$ use these identifications, and $F$ is any $A_X$-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Being in the image means being isomorphic to $i_*G$ for some $A_Z$-module sheaf $G$.

proof.text: First normalize the coefficient identifications. The formula in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] identifies $u^*M=u^{-1}M\otimes_{u^{-1}A_X,c_u}A_T$ with $u^{-1}M$ carrying the transported action $a\cdot m=c_u^{-1}(a)m$: the map is $m\otimes a\mapsto c_u^{-1}(a)m$, with inverse $m\mapsto m\otimes1$, and the balancing relation proves that they are inverse. Likewise transport an $A_Z$-module $G$ to an $i^{-1}A_X$-module by $b\cdot g=c_i(b)g$. Its direct-image $A_X$-action is unchanged, since the action through the adjoint of $c_i$ becomes the action through the inverse-image ring unit after this transport. These maps are natural in module maps; the adjunction bijections in the operations definition are consequently identified. More explicitly, let $T_i$ be this transport from $i^{-1}A_X$-modules to $A_Z$-modules and let $\theta_F:i^*F\xrightarrow{\sim}T_i(i^{-1}F)$ be the displayed tensor isomorphism. The identity of $i^*F$ corresponds, after transport, to $\theta_F^{-1}$. Transposing by the inverse-image adjunction gives $\eta_F^{c}=i_*(\theta_F^{-1})\circ\eta_F^{0}$, where $\eta^c$ is the specified module unit and $\eta^0$ the unit with inverse-image coefficients; hence $i_*(\theta_F)\circ\eta_F^c=\eta_F^0$. Thus invertibility of the actual unit is preserved. We may therefore work with $A_Z=i^{-1}A_X$, $A_U=j^{-1}A_X$, and $i^*=i^{-1}$, $j^*=j^{-1}$. This preserves zero objects, essential-image membership, and the specified unit map.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] with $A=A_X$. Its geometric hypotheses are exactly the closed immersion $i$ and its complementary quasi-compact open immersion $j$ in the item. It gives $j^{-1}i_*=0$, the adjunction $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$, and for every module sheaf $F$ the short exact sequence $0\to j_!j^{-1}F\to F\xrightarrow{\eta_F}i_*i^{-1}F\to0$. The middle-to-right arrow is the actual closed adjunction unit, not an unspecified map. The additional quasi-compact and quasi-separated hypothesis on $X$ in that node is only for its filtered-colimit clause, which is not used here.

proof.text: If $F\cong i_*G$, applying $j^{-1}$ to the isomorphism identifies $j^{-1}F$ with $j^{-1}i_*G=0$ by step 2. Thus every object in the essential image has zero open restriction.

source.place: Tag 09AH, lemma-ses-associated-to-open; arbitrary ring-sheaf version supplied by lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed

proof.text: Suppose $j^{-1}F=0$. By the adjunction of step 2, for every module sheaf $N$, $\operatorname{Hom}(j_!0,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(0,j^{-1}N)$ is a singleton. Thus $j_!0$ is initial and hence a zero object in the abelian module-sheaf category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The sequence in step 2 is consequently $0\to0\to F\xrightarrow{\eta_F}i_*i^{-1}F\to0$. By [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence], exactness at $F$ says $\ker\eta_F=0$, and the last zero says $\eta_F$ is epic. By the abelian-category definition [def-sp-abelian], the epimorphism $\eta_F$ is a cokernel of some map $h:T\to F$. Since $\eta_Fh=0$ and $\ker\eta_F=0$, the kernel universal property gives $h=0$. The cokernel universal property therefore factors $1_F$ uniquely as $r\circ\eta_F$ for a map $r:i_*i^{-1}F\to F$. Now $(\eta_F\circ r)\circ\eta_F=\eta_F$, so cancellation of the epimorphism gives $\eta_F\circ r=1_{i_*i^{-1}F}$. Thus $r$ is an explicit two-sided inverse of the actual unit. Step 1 carries this conclusion back to the originally specified coefficient identifications.

source.place: Tag 09AH, lemma-ses-associated-to-open; arbitrary ring-sheaf version supplied by lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed

proof.text: For $j^*F=0$, the inverse of the unit isomorphism in step 4 is an isomorphism $i_*i^*F\xrightarrow{\sim}F$, exhibiting $G=i^*F$ as a witness to essential-image membership. Conversely step 3 gives $j^*F=0$ for every such member. This proves both directions and the canonical-unit assertion.
